activity.title: We invited 199 founders to bring an egg to Cancun. They drew faces on them, named them, and carried them for 3 days through the airport, the pool, the catamaran, and by the sunset. It may sound silly, but it wasn't. Because the saying "don't put all your eggs in one basket" is the one rule founders intentionally break. One idea. One company. One bet that everyone warned us against. Then it gets even more complex. As you begin to grow, you ask others to put THEIR eggs in your basket too: their time, their careers, their trust. That’s the part nobody prepares you for. It’s not just the risk you take on yourself, it’s the responsibility for everyone who believes in you. For 3 days, 199 founders protected one fragile thing and ensured it didn’t crack. 100% survived. It turns out that’s the essence of the job: gather the right people in one place and ensure nothing breaks. That’s what we built Nowadays to do. And today, we’re launching the next chapter! An enterprise-grade Nowadays. The same self-serve, end-to-end AI event planning you already know, now designed to support an entire organization’s worth of eggs. One basket. Big enough for all of them 🥚

how would you get 199 eggs to cancun? pack them in your backpack and hope for the best? without the right protection, the right research, and a team you trust, someone's getting scrambled no egg left behind and here's the thing about eggs: they're fragile. and so is the opportunity. events are not just a to-do list item, they affect real people. the person with a life-threatening allergy who finally felt safe at an event the colleague who almost didn't come but made a lifelong friend. the offsite where someone decided to stay at the company another year. get it wrong and it's forgotten get it right and it becomes a tradition a memory people talk about years later that's the weight of it. and a lot of times this falls on one person. we know firsthand what it looks like when someone tries to juggle all the eggs themselves. the flights, the visa issues, the dietary needs, the room blocks. it only takes one crack. and when you're the one carrying all of it, you can't actually be present for the thing you planned. turns out, to get 199 eggs to cancun without cracking a single one… all you need is the right basket. today we're launching a new chapter of Nowadays . enterprise-grade, and built to carry all your eggs the same AI-powered event planning, now with self-serve so anyone can start without a call.

last week we brought 163 YC founders from 31 batches to Cancun for a YC alumni retreat. the words they used to describe it: electric. unforgettable. family. here's what we learned from pulling it off: 1/ the community is load-bearing. our YC partners pointed out that almost none of YC's billion-dollar companies disappeared after the batch. they stayed connected. they showed up to things. that's not a coincidence. we built this retreat because after the batch ends, that serendipity just stops – and we wanted to bring it back. 2/ the unplanned moments beat the planned ones. the late night mafia games in the presidential suite. the conversations that went until 2am. 100 founders spontaneously belting Linkin Park on a catamaran. we gave people time and space and enough structure to actually talk to each other, and they took it from there. 3/ the people are the product. 92% said they'd come back. but the most common open-ended response wasn't about the venue or the programming. it was about the quality of the founders in the room. that's the thing you can't manufacture. we're doing this again. June 2027, Cabo. aiming for a full hotel buyout so it's 100% founders on the property. if you want early access to tickets, link is in the comments 💛
9 months ago, amy and i walked a hotel in Cancun and had an idea it finally hatched 🐣 163 founders. 31 batches. S11 through W26. more to come :)

Stop dating. Start committing. The best advice is usually the kind we should take ourselves. That's what Nowadays is getting on stage to talk about at TAMS Ignite next week. And yes, it means exactly what you think it means -- for your travel and meetings program. Most companies have no idea how much they're spending on meetings. Not an estimate. Not a rough number. No idea. We worked with a top financial firm and found $18M in completely unmanaged meeting spend. Nobody knew it existed. And because nobody knew it existed, nobody could negotiate with it. When travel and meetings live in separate budgets, separate systems, separate conversations with hotels -- real money sits in the gap. Meetings are usually the first thing cut when budgets tighten. But cutting isn't the answer. Visibility is. The companies winning right now aren't spending less -- they're finally seeing the full picture and creating real value from what they already have. I sat in speaker prep today. The energy in that room was something. People who've spent decades on both sides of this problem, buyer and supplier, finally in the same conversation. Clearly a lot of love has gone into this. Emily Zhang and I are so ready. Boston and TAMS, see you Monday. Before we get there -- if you work in corporate travel or meetings: where does the misalignment hurt most? What's the cost nobody's putting a number on? Drop it below. We'll make sure to bring it to the room.

Every time, Anna Sun walks on stage and shares a bit about Nowadays , making the case for what AI can do for corporate travel and events. Yesterday she won the Business Travel Innovation Faceoff Award for the fifth time in a row. I get asked a lot what it's like to build a company with your sister. This is what it's like: watching her win over a crowd she's never met before, in city after city, for work you built together from scratch. Pretty special 🏆 Congratulations Anna Sun ! Time to go celebrate with some fish and chips :)
